what: Release-branch merge direction for aide-memory: always merge feature branches INTO `feature/phase-1` BEFORE tagging/publishing, not the other way. `feature/phase-1` is the canonical release line — every version tag must live on it. If a feature branch has diverged, the sequence is (1) merge feature-branch → feature/phase-1 on the release commit, (2) tag vX.Y.Z on the resulting phase-1 commit, (3) push. The 0.3.0 release accidentally did this backwards (merged phase-1 into feature/minified-publish, tagged and published from the feature branch, left origin/feature/phase-1 stale). The v0.3.0 tarball was still correct because all commits were included, but the branch topology was wrong and had to be retroactively fixed via `git push origin d02c783:refs/heads/feature/phase-1`. For future releases: the canonical flow in docs/RELEASING.md already describes this ordering — follow that, don't improvise.
why: User corrected this mid-session after 0.3.0 publish: "I thought we said merge prior to publish". The merge direction matters for branch topology cleanliness. Preserving so the next release doesn't make the same shortcut.
